name: BACH_0218
markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (94%)** · Confident · Careful review
Signals agree, but sampled regions show unusually many neoplastic nuclei.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 94%, InSitu 5% | Clear lead |
| Conformal set | {Benign} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.998 / 86th percentile | No input flag |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Weak support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 8) · ↓ invasive · Scarce; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F2] · Validated
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 7, 8, 9) · ↓ invasive · Prominent; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F4] · Validated
- **Tumor cell fraction and density** (regions 1, 5, 6) · context · 84% neoplastic nuclei (99th percentile); density 96th [F7, F8] · Measured

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI -0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. No cited concept is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- HoVer-Net shows 84% neoplastic nuclei in sampled regions; the Benign call may understate disease.
- Nearest cases split: 2 Benign, 2 InSitu, 1 Normal.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 5, 6** — highest invasive-logit contribution; confirm whether dense tumor nuclei are in situ or invasive.
2. **Region 1** — 134 neoplastic nuclei counted; check for duct-confined versus infiltrating growth.
3. **Regions 7, 8, 9** — confirm glands are benign and stroma shows no infiltration.
